many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import importlib.util
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('task',path)
mod=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
# Full synthesized demonstration grids from their solid-line / diagonal descriptions.
def stripes(n, lines):
    g=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    for r,v in lines.items(): g[r]=[v]*n
    return g
p1=stripes(15,{3:1,4:9,5:2,10:9})
e1=[[{0:9,1:2,2:9,3:1}[r%4]]*15 for r in range(15)]
p2=stripes(25,{12:6,13:1,15:9,20:5,22:9,23:3})
e2=[[{0:6,1:1,2:5,3:9,4:9,5:3}[r%6]]*25 for r in range(25)]
p3=[[0]*24 for _ in range(24)]
for r in range(19): p3[r][r+4]=5
for d,v in [(-18,6),(-19,2),(-20,5),(-22,7)]:
    for r in range(24):
        c=r+d
        if 0<=c<24: p3[r][c]=v
# Expected colors by d modulo 5: 0->5, 1->2, 2->6, 3->7, 4->5
phase={0:5,1:2,2:6,3:7,4:5}
e3=[[phase[(c-r)%5] for c in range(24)] for r in range(24)]
for i,(inp,exp) in enumerate([(p1,e1),(p2,e2),(p3,e3)],1):
    out=mod.transform(inp)
    print(i, out==exp)
# test input as supplied stripes
pt=[[0]*18 for _ in range(18)]
for r in range(5,18): pt[r][r-5]=5
for r in range(10,18): pt[r][r-10]=6
out=mod.transform(pt)
print('test result:')
print(out)
